title: Equal-weight marginal (Type III) tests in an unbalanced two-factor design
source_relation: adapted: new fixtures, function-style contract, independent cell-means oracle
difficulty_hypothesis: The default aov/anova table is sequential (Type I) and silently answers different hypotheses in an unbalanced design; drop1() on a default treatment-coded fit answers yet another question when an interaction is present; ordered factors switch to polynomial contrasts; and car::Anova, the usual shortcut, is not installed.

mcp_relevance.rationale: The task is statistical reasoning about hypotheses and contrast coding. The decisive facts (how contr.sum, drop1 scope and sequential SS behave) are in base R documentation that is also installed locally; no package version or ecosystem fact changes the answer.
mcp_relevance.information_need: Which linear hypotheses Type I/II/III sums of squares test, and how to obtain Type III values with base R only.
mcp_relevance.obtainable_without_mcp: yes: stats help pages (?drop1, ?contrasts, ?anova.lm) and the model-matrix algebra are available locally and in model knowledge
alternative_solution_paths: drop1(fit, scope = ~ ., test = 'F') on a contr.sum fit
explicit comparison of nested models built from effect-coded model matrices
cell-means linear-hypothesis (Wald/F) tests with equal-weight averaging

shared_features: Type I versus Type III hypotheses

calibration_risks.ceiling: moderate: strong models know the car::Anova idiom and the contr.sum + drop1 recipe
calibration_risks.floor: low: the output contract is fully specified

pinned_evidence.oracle: cell-means linear hypotheses L m = 0 with Var(m) = sigma^2 diag(1/n); self-checked against balanced anova() and against sequential SS at load time
